title: American Express Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Table 1: Summary of Financial Performance (p.44)
key_points: American Express reported an effective tax rate of 21.6% for the year ended December 31, 2022.
American Express reported an effective tax rate of 24.6% for the year ended December 31, 2021.
For comparison, the reported effective tax rate for 2020 was 27.0%.
In the same summary table, pretax income was $9,585 million in 2022 versus $10,689 million in 2021.
In the same summary table, the income tax provision was $2,071 million in 2022 versus $2,629 million in 2021.
The summary table's effective tax rate row carries no printed 'Change' column value, so no percentage-point change is stated by the filing in this table.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Note 20 Income Taxes: rate reconciliation table (statutory 21% to actual rate, 2022/2021/2020)
key_points: Rate reconciliation runs from U.S. statutory federal rate of 21.0% in all three years to actual tax rates of 21.6% (2022), 24.6% (2021) and 27.0% (2020), i.e. a 3.0 percentage-point year-over-year decline from FY2021 to FY2022.

Line 'Tax settlements and lapse of statute of limitations': (2.1)% in 2022 vs (0.3)% in 2021 vs (1.6)% in 2020 — a 1.8 pt swing toward favorable, the largest single-line movement between FY2021 and FY2022.
Line 'Non-U.S. subsidiaries' earnings': (0.1)% in 2022 vs 1.1% in 2021 vs 2.4% in 2020 — a 1.2 pt swing from a detriment to a small benefit.
Line 'Tax credits and tax-exempt income': (0.9)% in 2022 vs (0.1)% in 2021 vs (4.1)% in 2020 — a 0.8 pt increase in benefit.
Line 'State and local income taxes, net of federal benefit': 3.1% in 2022 vs 3.0% in 2021 vs 3.7% in 2020 — essentially flat year over year (+0.1 pt).
Line 'Valuation allowances': (0.1)% in 2022 vs —% in 2021 vs 4.0% in 2020 — FY2021 had no valuation-allowance effect on the ETR.
Line 'Other': 0.7% in 2022 vs (0.1)% in 2021 vs 1.6% in 2020 — a 0.8 pt unfavorable movement.

Footnote (a) on the reconciliation states it 'Includes the implementation of PAM related to investments in QAH projects for the year ended December 31, 2021' without identifying which reconciliation line it attaches to.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Note 20: changes in unrecognized tax benefits (settlements, statute lapse, interest and penalties)
key_points: Decreases from 'Settlements with tax authorities' were $74 million in 2022, versus $15 million in 2021 and $15 million in 2020.
Decreases from 'Lapse of statute of limitations' were $104 million in 2022, versus $17 million in 2021 and $58 million in 2020.
Combined settlements plus statute lapses reduced unrecognized tax benefits by $178 million in 2022 versus $32 million in 2021.
Unrecognized tax benefit balance was $962 million at December 31, 2022, down from $1,024 million at December 31, 2021 and up from $790 million at December 31, 2020.
Expense recognized for interest and penalties was approximately $10 million in 2022, $40 million in 2021 and $260 million in 2020.
Of the unrecognized tax benefits, approximately $750 million (2022), $780 million (2021) and $580 million (2020) would, if recognized, favorably affect the effective tax rate in a future period.
Accrual for payment of interest and penalties was approximately $380 million at both December 31, 2022 and December 31, 2021.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Table 1: Summary of Financial Performance (effective tax rate)
key_points: American Express's effective tax rate was 21.6% for FY2022, 24.6% for FY2021 and 27.0% for FY2020.
The FY2021→FY2022 change in AmEx's effective tax rate is a decline of 3.0 percentage points (24.6% → 21.6%).
AmEx's income tax provision fell from $2,629 million in FY2021 to $2,071 million in FY2022, a decrease of $558 million or 21%.
AmEx's pretax income fell from $10,689 million in FY2021 to $9,585 million in FY2022, a decrease of $1,104 million or 10%.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 20 Income Taxes: statutory-to-actual rate reconciliation
key_points: AmEx's rate reconciliation shows a U.S. statutory federal income tax rate of 21.0% in each of FY2022, FY2021 and FY2020 — i.e., the statutory rate was unchanged across the comparison period.
AmEx's actual tax rate was 21.6% in FY2022, which is 0.6 percentage points above the 21.0% statutory rate.
AmEx's actual tax rate was 24.6% in FY2021, which is 3.6 percentage points above the 21.0% statutory rate.
Tax settlements and lapse of statute of limitations reduced AmEx's rate by 2.1 points in FY2022 versus 0.3 points in FY2021.
Non-U.S. subsidiaries' earnings reduced AmEx's rate by 0.1 points in FY2022 versus increasing it by 1.1 points in FY2021.
Tax credits and tax-exempt income reduced AmEx's rate by 0.9 points in FY2022 versus 0.1 points in FY2021.
State and local income taxes, net of federal benefit, added 3.1 points in FY2022 versus 3.0 points in FY2021.

Total income tax expense was $2,071 million in FY2022 versus $2,629 million in FY2021; total current income tax expense was $3,260 million versus $2,335 million; total deferred income tax was a $(1,189) million benefit versus $294 million of expense.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — unrecognized tax benefits and future effective tax rate impact (p148)
key_points: Unrecognized tax benefits were $962 million at December 31, 2022 ($1,024M at 2021 year-end, $790M at 2020 year-end).
Of the $1.0 billion of unrecognized tax benefits at December 31, 2022, approximately $750 million, if recognized, would favorably affect the effective tax rate in a future period.

The company believes it is reasonably possible that unrecognized tax benefits could decrease within the next twelve months by as much as $150 million; approximately $118 million of that relates to amounts that, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate in a future period.
Interest and penalties on unrecognized tax benefits were approximately $10 million in 2022, $40 million in 2021 and $260 million in 2020.
